summary: Iteration 18: verified GET /api/admin/facebook/diagnose now includes the two new checks 'Token ↔ App match' and 'leads_retrieval permission' (via Meta debug_token). Diagnose returns 200 with checks=['Access Token','Token ↔ App match','leads_retrieval permission','Page subscribed to leadgen','App leadgen webhook'] and still exposes recent_webhook_deliveries. Regressions all green: invalid-sig webhook → 401 + 'rejected' log entry, /api/admin/facebook/webhook-log returns {count,logs} for admin and 401/403 without auth, backend healthy.
critical_code_review_comments: In fb_diagnose(), the debug_token block appends 'Token inspection' failure check only inside the except branch — if the /debug_token HTTP call succeeds but returns error payload (e.g. {"error":{...}} with empty data), dt is silently {} and NO check is appended, so 'Token ↔ App match' and 'leads_retrieval permission' would just be missing without any user-visible signal. Consider appending an explicit check when dt is empty or contains an error.

If app_id/app_secret are missing in settings, the two new checks are skipped silently. Consider adding an informational check like 'Token inspection skipped — App ID/Secret not configured' so users understand why the new diagnostics are absent.
seed_data_creation: One 'rejected' fb_webhook_log entry created via invalid-signature POST (capped at 200).
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter18 confirmed debug_token integration in diagnose(). In preview env, all 5 diagnose checks return ok=true (token is valid and matches app). Both new check names use the '↔' character — keep exact-match assertions consistent. Webhook log endpoint sort key 'at' is ISO-8601 string (lexicographic sort works). Test file auto-loads REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env when env var is not set.
